s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic systemic infection with granulomatous inflammation and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Progressively worsening fever, weight loss, night sweats, and dry cough
Painful nonhealing ulcer on the right hallux with necrotizing granulomatous inflammation
Chronic lower back pain with contiguous spondylitis and spinal cord compression
key_facts: Negative sputum GeneXpert tests at local clinics
Bilateral reticular-nodular opacities on chest radiograph
Induced sputum trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert
Biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus
MRI of the spine revealed contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Induced sputum trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert, biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus, and MRI of the spine revealed contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic systemic infection with granulomatous inflammation and multi-organ involvement, but less likely given the presence of acid-fast bacilli

shortlist.label: Mycobacterium avium complex infection
shortlist.why_kept: Similar symptoms to tuberculosis, but less likely given the specific identification of MTB in the sputum and biopsy

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and multi-organ involvement, but less likely given the absence of ANCA and the presence of acid-fast bacilli

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic systemic infection with granulomatous inflammation, but less likely given the presence of acid-fast bacilli and the specific gastrointestinal symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and test results, including a 2-year history of progressively worsening fever, weight loss, night sweats, and a dry cough, along with a positive sputum GeneXpert test for MTB, biopsy of the toe ulcer showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with an acid-fast bacillus, and MRI findings of contiguous spondylitis, are all consistent with disseminated tuberculosis.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: While sarcoidosis can cause granulomatous inflammation, the presence of acid-fast bacilli and positive MTB tests point more strongly towards tuberculosis.

rejected.label: Mycobacterium avium complex infection
rejected.why: This infection typically occurs in immunocompromised patients, and the test results specifically identified MTB, not Mycobacterium avium complex.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by vasculitis and the presence of anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), which were negative in this patient.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: While Crohn's disease can cause granulomatous inflammation, the systemic symptoms, positive MTB tests, and absence of gastrointestinal symptoms typical of Crohn's disease make this diagnosis less likely.
